Review catches structural/reasoning issues; the harness catches model-execution-fidelity issues invisible to review by a strong model, because a strong-model reviewer resolves the same ambiguity a strong-model author wrote it under. **Pre-ship = pre-push, and the gate is the *complete* suite on the cheapest practical model per engine, not a proportionate subset or an accidental expensive tier:** Claude Code -> haiku, Codex -> gpt-5.4-mini, Cursor -> composer-2.5. Run it in the background, wait, push only on green. Proportionality reasoning (\"this ship doesn't touch those procedures, so skip them\") is a review-time judgment, not a substitute for the gate. See `lifecycle-testing-harness.md`, `execution-testing-catches-blind-ambiguity.md`, `agent-boot-doc-fidelity-fixes.md`.\n- **Sandboxed-review blind spot (v28+)** — a review environment that structurally blocks a capability doesn't just miss findings in that area, it can green-light code whose primary path never executed. Concrete instance: a Codex review pass on Lore Beings' Keeper ran in a sandbox that blocked `ps`, so every PID-identity check took the \"unknown, can't verify\" branch — the confirmed-match/confirmed-mismatch logic never ran once, the suite went green, and a real bug (`macos-ps-o-multi-field-single-line.md`) survived until a fourth pass on real, unsandboxed macOS. Before trusting a green suite, check whether the review environment has a known-blocked capability the code under test depends on; if so, either re-run in an environment where it works, or confirm via the test's own branching that the \"unavailable\" path isn't silently substituting for the real one. This extends the empirical-pre-ship-verification framing above with an orthogonal axis (capability availability, not model tier). One confirmed instance of the *false-green* form — see `lore-beings-mvp-takeover-review.md`; promote to its own lore topic (candidate name `sandbox-degraded-review-blind-spot.md`) on a second independent occurrence of that form, per the name-foundational-principles bar. A related but distinct form is now recorded: a capability revoked *mid-run* makes results **uninterpretable** rather than falsely green (`macos-documents-permission-loss-mid-session.md`, v30) — same reflex (check the environment before believing the verdict), different failure mode, so it does not yet count as the second occurrence.\n- **Standing improvement list maintenance (v27+)** — maintain `workdir/what-to-improve.md` as an always-current, prioritized action list for framework improvements, distinct from `framework-improvements-backlog.md` (the canonical unranked store with full detail). The standing list is the ranked action view: reread it at the start of every framework-work session, work it down, refresh it (re-rank, insert new findings, delete-don't-mark shipped/moot items) at each architecture review. User-established practice, 2026-07-18 — the explicit intent is that a list of this shape *always exists*, not that one gets produced once per review. See `standing-improvement-list-practice.md`.\n\nThese disciplines compose: a version ship is the moment when (a) release notes get the cache-clear footer if cache-affecting, (b) `versioning-release-types.md` history gets the new entry with cache-affecting annotation, (c) all version-bearing plugin manifests get bumped to `1.<VERSION>.0`, (d) any newly-discovered foundational principle from the design discussion gets its own topic, and (e) touched procedures get their lifecycle scenarios run, not just reviewed.\n\n## How You Work\n\nYou work across two repositories:\n- **`lore-framework/`** — where the framework plugin lives (a Claude Code plugin with prefix `lr`). When evolving the system, changes go here.\n- **`lore-framework-dev/`** — a dedicated agent repo for lore framework development. Houses this agent (lore-architect) and its lore, workdir, and sessions, plus dev-only tests (`tests/`, including the multi-engine lifecycle testing harness under `tests/lifecycle/`) — kept here rather than in the plugin so the plugin stays slim. Separate from `lore-agents/` (which hosts personal agents — tax-advisor, masschallenge-judge) so that framework design knowledge accumulates as a team-shared resource rather than a personal one. See `plugin-vs-agent-repo-separation.md`.\n\nWhen working on the framework, use `claude --plugin-dir ./lore-framework` from the workspace root, or have it installed via the marketplace.\n\nWhen the user discusses design changes, new features, or issues with the lore system, you help think through the implications, draft updates to framework files, and keep the design coherent.\n\nYou are both a user and a builder of this system — you use lore to track your own knowledge about the system you're building.\n# Lore Context\n\nCompacted working knowledge for the **lore-architect**. This is the entry point to the lore graph, not a catalog — each theme points at its summary topic, which fans out to detail. For exhaustive lookup, scan `lore/` directly. (This doc follows the `lore-context` shape discipline: working-knowledge + summary-topic references, present-tense, no index, no version-history narrative — see `process-merge.md` § Step 4.)\n\n## Style Skills\n\nA category of user-invoked `/lr:` skill that changes how the agent *communicates or collaborates* (vs. operations like `/lr:recall`/`/lr:merge`). Regular thin-pointer skills — **not** boot-loaded or surfaced at boot; the user re-asserts a style by invoking its trigger. Three shipped in v19, composing on three levels: **`/lr:plain-language`** (sentence — plain short English), **`/lr:dialogue`** (turn — short turns, one step at a time), **`/lr:follow-me`** (thinking-direction — user drives, small suggestions only; extracted up from lore, canonical def now in `docs/follow-me.md`). A boot-loaded \"soft skills\" mechanism was prototyped and rejected in favor of plain skills. See `style-skills.md`, `skill-request-defaults-to-regular-skill.md`, `soft-skill-follow-me-mode.md`.\n\n## Who I Am\n\nArchitect and maintainer of the lore system — the `lr` framework plugin and the agent ecosystem on it. I work across two repos: **`lore-framework/`** (the distributed plugin — changes to how agents work go here) and **`lore-framework-dev/`** (my own agent repo — my lore, workdir, sessions). I'm both builder and user: I use lore to track my own design knowledge. See `role.md`.\n\n## System Architecture\n\nThree discrete layers — identify which one owns a change before touching files:\n1. **Plugin** (`lore-framework/`, installed as `lr`) — what's distributed via the marketplace: skills, docs, migrations, scripts, manifests, `VERSION`. Universal across installs.\n2. **Domain** — the conceptual scope of one agent repo, marked by `lore-repo.md` (frontmatter: `description`, `version`, optional `repos:`). Holds `agents/<name>/` with `role.md`, `lore-context.md`, `lore/`, `workdir/`, `sessions/`.\n3. **Workspace** — the filesystem Claude runs from; holds one or more agent repos + their declared siblings. Discovery scans workspace-root dirs for `lore-repo.md`; nested repos are invisible to most skills.\n\nSee `architecture-overview.md`, `workspace-vs-domain-vocabulary.md`, `agent-discovery-nesting-constraint.md`, `plugin-vs-agent-repo-separation.md`.\n\n## Design Principles\n\nIdentity-layer framings that frame everything else:\n- **Team-shared knowledge** — agents are team-shared knowledge containers, not personal notebooks. Design for concurrent multi-contributor use.\n- **Engine, not KB** — the framework is the engine/environment for self-improving agents; the knowledge base is a consequence, not the identity.\n- **Executors first, advisors second** — primary value is getting things done; conversation is secondary. The usage→learning positive feedback loop only spins under executor-first framing.\n\nWhat each agent carries: **knowledge** (markdown — what it knows, accrues passively via reflection) + **skills** (tools + instructions — what it can do, evolves actively via in-flight teaching). Distinct assets; don't collapse them.\n\nCore mechanics: directory-driven, plain markdown (frontmatter only on descriptor files), git-as-metadata, delete-don't-mark, knowledge graph by filename reference, concise context with detail on demand, skill/doc separation, repo-level versioning. Framework owns the universal; agents own repo/host/workflow specifics.\n\n**Subagent as optimization vs subagent as semantics** — before letting any engine degrade a\nsubagent-spawning procedure to serial host-side execution, classify what the subagent is *for*. If it\nbuys parallelism and context isolation (recall, consult, attach, merge, conflict resolution),\nserialization is lossless. If the subagent's *independence from the caller* is the deliverable\n(`/lr:trilens-loop`), serialization destroys the feature — the procedure must stop and report. Profile\ndegradation clauses therefore need carve-outs, not blanket rules, and \"the conservative profile passed\nthe whole suite\" only ever meant it was adequate for the procedures that existed then. See\n`subagent-as-optimization-vs-subagent-as-semantics.md`.\n\nSee `system-design-principles.md` (the full list and the overreach diagnostics), plus the framing topics `team-shared-knowledge-principle.md`, `framework-as-engine-not-kb.md`, `agents-are-executors-first.md`, `knowledge-vs-skills-distinction.md`, `framework-scope-vs-agent-scope.md`.\n\n## Skills & Docs\n\nOperations are Claude Code plugin skills, `lr:` prefix on Claude; Cursor uses `/lr-<skill>` via\nprefixed wrappers (`cursor-dual-skill-tree-one-repo.md`). **Skills are thin pointers** — each `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` is a one-line reference to `docs/<name>.md`, where all logic lives. Same for generated `/lr-<agent>-agent` boot commands (thin delegations to `agent-boot.md`). When a skill orchestrates sub-skills, the orchestration gets its own `docs/<skill>.md`; non-skill procedures shared across call sites get a `docs/<procedure>.md` (e.g. `auto-pull.md`). See `slash-command-system.md`, `skill-doc-pattern.md`, `shared-procedure-doc-pattern.md`, `single-canonical-source-discipline.md`.\n\nAn **accelerator** script (Script Fallback Contract) can go one step further and become\n**literate**: the procedure lives in the script's own instructional comments rather than in a\ncompanion doc, so there's one artifact instead of two that can drift apart. First applied to\n`scripts/lr-core` in v31. Hard constraint at that seam: **the script emits data, the doc owns\nuser-facing words** — a script string that reads like a finished message gets printed as one, and\nprinting it *looks* like hand…2693 tokens truncated…separate single-lens, role-as-perspective tool for high-stakes single edits. See `trilens-loop-feature.md`, `parallel-reviewer-fanout-pattern.md`, `sonnet-subagent-review-pattern.md`. **Second, empirical leg (v18+):** for procedure docs covered by the lifecycle testing harness, also run the relevant scenarios against real engine execution before shipping — review catches reasoning issues, the harness catches model-execution-fidelity issues invisible to a strong-model reviewer — and the fidelity axis is **engine, not just model tier** (run scenarios on every engine, using the cheapest practical default tier unless explicitly overriding: Claude Code -> haiku, Codex -> gpt-5.4-mini, Cursor -> composer-2.5; the same model tier can behave differently by engine, and mid-procedure step insertions are the highest-risk for a silent skip). See `lifecycle-testing-harness.md`, `execution-testing-catches-blind-ambiguity.md`, `haiku-ambiguity-detector.md`.\n- **A gate result belongs to an artifact state** — a converged review loop and a green lifecycle run each certify only the tree they actually ran against. An edit landed after the gates pass is ungated: re-run the affected gate, or revert and file a follow-up. Never report \"converged and green\" for a tree neither gate saw, and record *which* state a result belongs to. Also: an environment failure mid-run (e.g. macOS TCC revocation) or the engine resolving a *different* plugin tree makes results **uninterpretable**, not red — fix and re-run rather than debugging the code under test. See `post-convergence-edits-need-their-own-gate.md`, `macos-documents-permission-loss-mid-session.md`.\n- **A gate cannot be a model self-report** — a gate must not be implemented in the medium it gates. Ask what evidence it rests on and whether the thing under test could have produced that evidence; if yes, it is a self-report wearing a gate's name. \"Both engines have coverage\" is not evidence parity. See `a-gate-cannot-be-a-model-self-report.md`.\n- **A failure list is a hypothesis until someone reads the transcripts** — an assertion message names what was observed, never why. Re-triage from stored logs before planning fixes; stored artifacts plus `stat` routinely beat fresh engine probes on cost and certainty. Classify each text assertion as mid-run (needs the transcript) or end-state (final message suffices) — mixing them changes what a test means per engine. See `v31-lifecycle-rerun-partial-green-2026-07-27.md`, `transcript-vs-final-message-assertions.md`.\n- **Decide where the guardrail lives before writing the topic** — lore is retrieved when a task cues it, and a one-off command cues nothing; a trap recorded only as knowledge protects nobody, including its author. Name the point-of-use site (script check, exact command in the doc, test) as part of the fix, and prefer a deterministic harness check over a human prep step. See `point-of-use-guardrails-beat-recorded-lore.md`, `docs-engines-convention.md` § Engine traps belong in the binding.\n- **Verify before asserting** — check filesystem/state directly before \"fixing\" a suspected bug; verify *which* bug, not just whether. **Pointed inward:** before declaring a known finding moot — especially a ship-blocking one — read the lore rule it rests on rather than reconstructing it; reconstruction keeps a rule's motivating case and drops its actual obligation, and those diverge precisely when dismissal feels justified (`check-own-lore-before-dismissing-a-finding.md`). Same reflex, two more sites: fetch volatile external facts (prices, model IDs, rate limits) live with a dated citation rather than trusting memory — \"couldn't verify\" licenses marking a value unavailable, not guessing; and after any scoped/read-only subagent or fork returns, verify its actual filesystem footprint (`git status`, `git worktree list`) rather than trusting its summary — a capable fork acts on the largest goal it can see in inherited context unless scoped *against* it explicitly. See `verify-before-acting-on-suspected-bugs.md`, `fetch-volatile-facts-live-not-memory.md`, `fork-scope-creep-under-standing-goal.md`.\n- **Curation meta-rules:** name foundational principles as their own topics; single canonical source (pointer, don't restate — and its design-time cousin: reuse an existing correlation/identity signal before inventing new plumbing); don't defer completable bounded sweeps; graduated verification (confidence, not boolean). See `naming-foundational-principles.md`, `single-canonical-source-discipline.md`, `reuse-existing-correlation-signal.md`, `feedback-don-t-defer-completable-scope.md`, `graduated-verification-confidence.md`.\n- **User-feedback working style:** ranked-shortlist over exhaustive enumeration; confirm before writing durable lore mid-session; in design dialogues, write the draft only when the user triggers it (decisions are safe in conversation — don't repeatedly move to persist); populate dry-run counters with would-be outcomes; \"enforce X\" ≠ add a required schema field; for broad/emotionally-loaded open-ended asks, decompose into hidden axes and sequence a build order by dependency (cheapest/highest-leverage first, flashiest/most-structural last) rather than proposing a menu or jumping to implementation; on a second round of pushback on the same axis (length, tone, scope), act on the next ask instead of re-justifying — a second \"no\" is not a request for more reasoning; a **short measurement question gets a short factual answer**, with the interesting generalisation offered rather than delivered, and **several style skills invoked at once is a stop signal**, not a preference tweak (hold the style for the rest of the session). See `feedback-too-many-words.md`, `feedback-confirm-before-writing-lore.md`, `feedback-draft-only-when-user-triggers.md`, `feedback-schemas-as-enforcement-overreach.md`, `feedback-layered-decomposition-for-open-ended-asks.md`, `feedback-mvp-minimalism.md`, `feedback-comply-promptly-after-repeated-pushback.md`.\n\n## Key Constraints\n\n- `lore-context.md` ≤ 50K tokens; **shape over size** — working-knowledge + summary-topic references, not an index (see `lore-context-shape-discipline.md`).\n- Lore topics: atomic, <5K tokens preferred, plain markdown, no frontmatter.\n- Descriptor frontmatter: `lore-repo.md` = `description` + `version` (+ optional `repos:`); `role.md` = `description` only.\n- Command filenames: lowercase/digits/hyphens, ≤64 chars.\n- Placeholders: `<workspace>`, `<lore-agent-repo>`, `<guest-lore-agent-repo>`, `<agent-name>`, `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`.\n- **CWD safety:** never `cd` when later tools depend on cwd — use `git -C <repo>`. **Portable shell:** assume BSD/macOS, no GNU-only binaries (`timeout`); bound commands via the Bash-tool timeout.\n- See `conventions.md`, `placeholder-vocabulary.md`, `tooling-cwd-safety.md`, `portable-shell-in-framework-docs.md`.\n\n## Onboarding-Doc Authoring\n\nCo-authoring framework onboarding docs for adopting teams is part of the role. Two distinct genres now exist: **`onboarding-doc-narrative-pattern.md`** (long-form prose pitching a human reader) and **`paste-link-installer-doc-genre.md`** (a doc written *to the AI agent* as the literal installer, meant to be pasted as a link — shipped as `QUICKSTART.md` + per-engine `INSTALL-<ENGINE>.md`). Load the identity-layer framings first, then the toolkit: the two genre topics above, `use-cases-via-parallel-consult-pattern.md`, `terminology-domain-collision-trap.md`, `agent-as-universal-working-environment.md`, `in-flight-skill-teaching-pattern.md`. Pre-ship review for either genre uses `parallel-reviewer-fanout-pattern.md`'s multi-lens fan-out; the installer genre additionally needs the **AI-installer (literal executor)** lens (`ai-installer-review-lens.md`) — it catches execution-fidelity bugs (e.g. `skill-doc-filename-divergence-bug-class.md`) the newcomer/editorial lenses miss. Landing-page placement of a self-referential/meta example differs from long-narrative placement — primacy goes to the strongest CTA; see `onboarding-doc-narrative-pattern.md` § placement note. A recurring funnel bug: an author writing from the fresh-start perspective railroads readers into create-your-first-agent and leaves the **team-join path** invisible at every layer (README prose, QUICKSTART, and the INSTALL AI-agent preambles) — check all layers, and keep the fork question verbatim-identical across sites (`onboarding-funnel-team-join-path.md`). Adopter-facing prose carries the product name **\"Lore Agents\"** while the engine keeps `lore-framework`/`lr` (`lore-agents-product-name.md`). First instance: the Activities team's intro doc.\n\n## Active Design Explorations\n\n- **lr-dev / Dark Factory (DF)** — major direction; a `lr` module for SDLC automation toward an autonomous \"dark factory\" SDLC. Per-repo artifacts + narrative context live in a `<repo>-df` backbone (a `repo-lore/<file>/` mirror: `file-lore.md` narrative landing + flat structured aspect subdirs like `ula/`). Skills not agents; persistence external. First aspect: **AIQA/ULA** (`/lr:df-repo-init`, `/lr:df-ula-file`) — unit-level analysis with a bug-verification track, BETA. The DF/ULA design thread is closed and the module ships as BETA. Anchor: `lr-dev-direction.md`; see `df-per-repo-backbone.md`, `aiqa-ula-feature.md`, `df-module-conventions.md`, `workflow-primitive-operational-notes.md`.\n- **Autonomous agents / Lore Beings** — agents as always-on background collaborators with persistent task state, raising for input only when needed. Concrete steps taken: `/lr:spawn-teammate` (multi-agent substrate, v10) and the v18 **`lr-wait`** primitive — the first *inbound-signal* step: an agent blocks on an event and an external actor (cron/CI/webhook/human, via `lr-emit`) wakes it with text. **The beings design is settled (2026-07-19): the module is _Lore Beings_.** A being is an ordinary lore agent plus a `being.md` descriptor; the **Being Keeper** (`lrb`) is deterministic substrate (never an LLM). **MVP is CLI-only**; engines are explicit user config. Budget = daily-USD spawn gate + per-task wall-clock kill. **Engine kinds: `claude`, `codex`, and `cursor`** — cursor landed in framework v28: requires `--plugin-dir` at `engines add`, claude-shaped JSON result + flat-cost fallback. **Keeper-specific real-engine lifecycle coverage now exists** (`tests/lifecycle/keeper_harness.py` + `test_lrb_lifecycle.py`, 10 scenarios after the 2026-07-20 fifth pass added B2/B3, separate higher-blast-radius gate `LR_LIFECYCLE_KEEPER=1`, verified claude 6/6 + codex 1/1 + cursor 1/1 at the recommended-minimum tier). That fifth pass found and fixed a real production bug, not just a coverage gap: `cursor-agent`'s sandboxed shell tool escapes `_kill`'s `killpg` by running spawned commands in a freshly `setsid`'d session, which left a real orphaned process on the test machine before the fix — `_kill` now also walks the full ppid-descendant tree and signals every descendant directly, enumerated *before* any ancestor is signaled (killing the ancestor first risks the OS reparenting a survivor to PID 1 and erasing the ppid link). **The Keeper substrate shipped BETA in v28, and v29 added the in-engine command surface `/lr:being`** — one skill with subcommands (status/init/create/validate/logs/keeper/engine/workspace/pause/resume) over the same deterministic `lrb` CLI, rather than a `lrb-*` skill per operation. Ship record: v28 at framework commit `5e00209`, tag `lr--v1.28.0`; the standard lifecycle gate passed by persisted broad matrix plus targeted reruns. Real-engine verification sharpened two per-kind contract gaps (both backlog schema decisions, not silently patched): the `cursor` kind is empirically cost-blind (no `total_cost_usd`), so its flat `--session-cost-usd` fallback is load-bearing not optional; the `claude` kind has no `--plugin-dir` field, so a claude-kind being needs a wrapper-script `command` to load `lr:` skills at all. Two further findings from that same review pass — budget-enforcement edge cases and an unattended-full-permission trust gap — were deliberately deferred to the backlog rather than fixed. Chronicler week-long soak and persistent `--launchd` install still user-triggered. Open gap: headless permissions (`permission_mode: full` vs future scoped-tools), and self-scheduling under the safe default. What made this tractable: the knowledge substrate (agent\n  repos, `lore-repo.md`, `role.md`, `lore/`, `lore-context.md`, git) was already engine-agnostic, so\n  the port was **packaging, not redesign** — the whole surface is **5 adapter bindings** via the\n  `docs/engines/` convention (framework-root, invocation-syntax, subagent-spawn, memory-file,\n  runtime-bounding) plus Boot Step-0 engine selection. Both engines have native in-session subagents\n  (Codex `spawn_agent`/`wait_agent`; Cursor `Task`), so the feared Tier-B nucleus is proven, and one\n  repo carries both skill namespaces (canonical `skills/<skill>/` for Claude, `.cursor-skills/lr-<skill>/`\n  wrappers for Cursor, kept in sync by `scripts/sync-cursor-skills` and `/lr:check` #21).\n\n  Standing operational facts worth carrying: **trust rollout/tool-call logs, not model self-report**,\n  when validating an engine path; Codex's default sandbox blocks `.git` writes and network, so the\n  supported finalization path needs `.git` writable through launch/config (a commit-blocked run is\n  degraded fallback, not a merge failure); Codex per-agent shortcut register/unregister/list remains an\n  unvalidated implementation gap. The **\"framework is prose executed by the model\"** risk is\n  empirically retired for the exercised paths, and the substrate half has quantitative backing — the\n  quality benchmark showed positive lore-utilization uplift on every engine+model config, with the\n  nuance that **model–engine fit beats model tier**. Cross-engine support is a *supporting* fact in\n  positioning, not the headline (the 2026-07-20 landscape re-survey found competitors claiming it too);\n  lead with the triad. See\n  `v25-workspace-pull-init-design.md`, `workspace-meta-repo-pattern.md`.\n\n## Current State\n\nWorkspace holds three canonical repos: **`lore-framework/`** (plugin), **`lore-framework-dev/`**\n(this repo — lore-architect lore, tests, drafts), and **`lore-agents/`** (personal agents).\n\n`lore-framework/` is **clean and pushed at v31** on `main`. Concrete steps taken: `/lr:spawn-teammate` (multi-agent substrate, v10) and the v18 **`lr-wait`** primitive — the first *inbound-signal* step: an agent blocks on an event and an external actor (cron/CI/webhook/human, via `lr-emit`) wakes it with text. **The beings design is settled (2026-07-19): the module is _Lore Beings_.** A being is an ordinary lore agent plus a `being.md` descriptor; the **Being Keeper** (`lrb`) is deterministic substrate (never an LLM). **MVP is CLI-only**; engines are explicit user config. Budget = daily-USD spawn gate + per-task wall-clock kill. **Engine kinds: `claude`, `codex`, and `cursor`** — cursor landed in framework v28: requires `--plugin-dir` at `engines add`, claude-shaped JSON result + flat-cost fallback. **Keeper-specific real-engine lifecycle coverage now exists** (`tests/lifecycle/keeper_harness.py` + `test_lrb_lifecycle.py`, 10 scenarios after the 2026-07-20 fifth pass added B2/B3, separate higher-blast-radius gate `LR_LIFECYCLE_KEEPER=1`, verified claude 6/6 + codex 1/1 + cursor 1/1 at the recommended-minimum tier). That fifth pass found and fixed a real production bug, not just a coverage gap: `cursor-agent`'s sandboxed shell tool escapes `_kill`'s `killpg` by running spawned commands in a freshly `setsid`'d session, which left a real orphaned process on the test machine before the fix — `_kill` now also walks the full ppid-descendant tree and signals every descendant directly, enumerated *before* any ancestor is signaled (killing the ancestor first risks the OS reparenting a survivor to PID 1 and erasing the ppid link). **The Keeper substrate shipped BETA in v28, and v29 added the in-engine command surface `/lr:being`** — one skill with subcommands (status/init/create/validate/logs/keeper/engine/workspace/pause/resume) over the same deterministic `lrb` CLI, rather than a `lrb-*` skill per operation. Ship record: v28 at framework commit `5e00209`, tag `lr--v1.28.0`; the standard lifecycle gate passed by persisted broad matrix plus targeted reruns. Real-engine verification sharpened two per-kind contract gaps (both backlog schema decisions, not silently patched): the `cursor` kind is empirically cost-blind (no `total_cost_usd`), so its flat `--session-cost-usd` fallback is load-bearing not optional; the `claude` kind has no `--plugin-dir` field, so a claude-kind being needs a wrapper-script `command` to load `lr:` skills at all. Two further findings from that same review pass — budget-enforcement edge cases and an unattended-full-permission trust gap — were deliberately deferred to the backlog rather than fixed. Chronicler week-long soak and persistent `--launchd` install still user-triggered. ### 22. Assistant — 2026-07-28T03:05:29.119Z

Yes. The shortcut can be version-agnostic; the current v31 template simply chose an absolute cache path as its bootstrap mechanism.

Codex does not expose a stable `…/lr/latest/` path for this plugin, so the robust design is a small version-independent resolver:

1. The agent shortcut identifies the installed `lr` plugin directory dynamically.
2. It verifies the candidate contains `VERSION` and `docs/agent-boot.md`.
3. It reads that file and continues boot.
4. If multiple installed copies are ambiguous, it stops instead of guessing.

That lets every existing shortcut survive upgrades and rollbacks. I’d make this a shared Codex bootstrap convention, so individual agent shortcuts stay one-line pointers to it—not each implementing cache discovery.

The alternative is a `latest` symlink maintained on installation, but that depends on Codex/plugin-install support and is less portable. The resolver is the right framework-level fix.

Session Context That Shapes Relevance\n\nTwo to five bullets covering decisions made, constraints surfaced, paths or filenames being touched, open questions. This is what lets the subagent distinguish *relevant* from *generally related*.\n\n### 3. The Angle — If You Have One\n\nIf the user provided a hint (`/lr:recall anything about versioning`), center the brief on it.\n\nIf not, describe the *kind* of lore that would help — prior decisions, operational lessons, domain facts, known pitfalls, past trade-offs. This anchors the subagent's reading.\n\n### 4. The Output Shape You Want Back\n\nAsk explicitly for:\n- A compact synthesis (under ~400 words) grouped by theme\n- Each finding tagged with its source topic filename\n- Explicit call-outs for topics worth reading in full yourself\n- *\"Nothing relevant found\"* if that's the honest answer — don't invent relevance\n\nKeep the whole brief under ~300 words. The subagent has access to your full `lore/` directory; you don't need to summarize what's *in* lore, only what's in *this session*.\n\n## Worked Example\n\n**Brief sent to the subagent:**\n\n> Search the lore at `agents/lore-architect/lore/` for topics relevant to my current task.\n>\n> **Task:** Designing a `/lr:recall` skill that lets the user explicitly trigger a lore search mid-session. The synthesis is inlined into the main agent's working context.\n>\n> **Session context:**\n> - Decided against introducing a vector DB at current scale — using LLM-driven subagent scan instead\n> - Framework bumping to v3 with new search guidance and a recall skill\n> - Keeping `agent-boot.md` compact — detailed search guidance lives in a separate doc\n> - Following the existing skill/doc separation pattern\n>\n> **Looking for:** prior decisions on user-invocable skills, transparency patterns (showing intermediate results to the user), past discussion of subagent usage in the framework.\n>\n> **Output:** compact synthesis grouped by theme, ≤400 words, with topic filenames. Flag anything I should read in full. Say \"nothing relevant\" if true.\n\n**Expected response shape:**\n\n> **User-invocable skill conventions** (`slash-command-system.md`): all user-invocable skills use the `/lr:` prefix; generated artifacts use `/lr-`. Skill files are thin pointers; logic lives in `docs/`.\n>\n> **Skill/doc separation** (`skill-doc-pattern.md`): every skill is one line pointing at `<framework-root>/docs/<name>.md`. Recall should follow this exactly.\n>\n> **No prior recall pattern** — no existing topic discusses user-triggered context enrichment. New ground.\n>\n> **Read in full:** `slash-command-system.md` for the conventions you'll be following.\n\n## What to Do With the Result\n\n1. **Show the synthesis to the user.** Transparency — they should see what got pulled in and judge whether the recall was useful. If multiple active agents were scanned (fan-out), group results by agent so it's clear whose lore each finding came from.\n2. **Carry it as working context** for the rest of the session.\n3. **Read flagged topics in full yourself** — don't trust synthesis alone for load-bearing details.\n\n## Direct-Tool Fallback\n\nWhen you know exactly what you're looking for or just need a quick check, the standard tools are fine — no subagent needed:\n\n- **Glob / list** — see what topics exist\n- **Grep** — search for a specific keyword across topics\n- **Read** — read a specific topic in full\n- **`git log`** — when a topic was created (`git -C <lore-agent-repo> log --diff-filter=A -- agents/<agent-name>/lore/<topic>.md`), last updated (`git -C <lore-agent-repo> log -1 -- agents/<agent-name>/lore/<topic>.md`), or full history (`git -C <lore-agent-repo> log --follow -- agents/<agent-name>/lore/<topic>.md`). Use `git -C` rather than `cd`ing into the repo — the shell CWD is shared with Glob and Grep.\n- **Deleted topics** remain in git history — searchable if you need past knowledge that was later removed\n\nRule of thumb: use the subagent when you're searching by **meaning**; use direct tools when you're searching by **name** or **exact term**.\n# WHAT TO IMPROVE — Standing Improvement List\n\nThe standing, prioritized improvement list for the Lore Agents framework. Established\n2026-07-18 at the user's request, with the explicit intent that a list of this type\n**always exists** — a continuous-improvement instrument for the framework, not a one-off\nreview artifact. Work it down across sessions; refresh it with each new review.\n\n**Relationship to `framework-improvements-backlog.md` (lore):** the backlog is the\ncanonical *unranked* store of deferred items, grouped by area, with full detail. This file\nis the *ranked action view* — what to do next and why, in priority order. Items here carry\na couple of sentences plus pointers; deep detail stays in the backlog entry or lore topic\nthey reference. The two must not fork: when an item's detail grows, it goes to the backlog\nor a topic, and this file keeps the one-liner + pointer.\n\n## Refresh Protocol\n\n- Reread at the start of every framework-work session; the priorities here frame what to\n  pick up next unless the user directs otherwise.\n- Full refresh at each periodic architecture review (last: 2026-07-18). A refresh re-ranks\n  surviving items, inserts new findings in rank order, and deletes shipped/moot entries\n  (git history preserves them — delete-don't-mark).\n- When an item ships: mark `✅ done <date>, <version/commit>` inline, delete on the next\n  refresh.\n- Evidence discipline: items born from a review cite the evidence (what was measured or\n  observed), so a later session can re-verify rather than trust a stale claim.\n\n## Verdict of the 2026-07-18 Review\n\nArchitecture is coherent and disciplined: the three-layer model is clean, skill→doc\npattern mostly honored, v27 stamps/manifests/cursor-parity all consistent, docs lean\n(~4.2K lines). Two structural risks: **(1) mechanical procedures executed as LLM\ninstructions don't hold at current scale** — a deterministic sweep found 14 unresolved\nlore cross-references that `/lr:check` #9–10 nominally cover; **(2) no subtraction force**\n— the rot predicted by the consolidation/\"sleep\" thread is now measured, not hypothetical.\nBiggest UX gap: agents only remember when *asked* — ambient recall and friction-free\ncapture would change how the system feels more than anything else here.\n\n---\n\n## A. The Remedy below still applies — clear the cache directly, restart Claude Code, then re-attempt `/lr:doctor` to verify.\n\n## Symptoms\n\n- A skill known to exist in the current framework `VERSION` does not appear in the session's available-skills list (e.g. `/lr:workspace-pull` is missing on a v25+ install).\n- An **old** skill name still appears after a hard rename (e.g. `/lr:workspace-sync` is still listed after the v25 rename to `/lr:workspace-pull`).\n- A SKILL.md or doc edit made in the marketplace install at `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/lore-framework/`, or via a normal plugin update, doesn't seem to have taken effect — the prior content keeps loading.\n- A registered per-agent shortcut (`/lr-<agent-name>-agent` on Claude Code, `$lr-<agent-name>-agent` on Codex) points at a path or behavior that no longer matches the framework — typically right after upgrading.\n- A `/plugin update` or marketplace refresh appears to succeed but Claude Code's behavior reflects the prior version.\n- An expected **MCP server's tools do not appear** after an upgrade (e.g. `lr-wait`'s `wait_for_event` / `sleep` are missing) — the cache holds the prior plugin tree without the new `.mcp.json` / server. (If instead the server is present but failing to launch, that is not a cache issue — check its runtime is installed, e.g. `python3` on `PATH` for `lr-wait`.)\n\n## Diagnosis\n\n1. **Confirm the framework `VERSION`.**\n\n   ```bash\n   cat ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/lore-framework/VERSION\n   ```\n\n   If the source-of-truth `VERSION` reflects what's expected, the framework files on disk are current — the issue is then almost certainly cached state in the running Claude Code session.\n\n2. **Inspect the cache structure.** Plugin caches live under `~/.claude/plugins/cache/`. The top-level entries are marketplace names; one or two levels deeper you find per-plugin version directories. List the structure:\n\n   ```bash\n   find ~/.claude/plugins/cache -maxdepth 3 -type d\n   ```\n\n3. **Cross-check the cached version against the marketplace install.** The marketplace files (the upstream \"truth\") live under `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/lore-framework/`. Compare cached `VERSION` to marketplace `VERSION`:\n\n   ```bash\n   ls ~/.claude/plugins/cache/lore-framework/lr/\n   for v in ~/.claude/plugins/cache/lore-framework/lr/*/; do\n     echo \"cache: $(basename \"$v\") -> VERSION=$(cat \"$v/VERSION\" 2>/dev/null)\"\n   done\n   echo \"marketplace: VERSION=$(cat ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/lore-framework/VERSION)\"\n   ```\n\n   Then diff the skill catalogs. If `lr/` contains exactly one version directory, the simpler form works; if multiple version directories coexist, pick the one Claude Code is actually loading from `installed_plugins.json`:\n\n   ```bash\n   # Single-version case:\n   LR_CACHE_VER=$(ls ~/.claude/plugins/cache/lore-framework/lr/ | sort -V | tail -1)\n   diff -r ~/.claude/plugins/cache/lore-framework/lr/$LR_CACHE_VER/skills/ \\\n           ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/lore-framework/skills/ | head\n   ```\n\n4. **The deciding signal:** the symptom (e.g. a v11-only skill missing from the available-skills list) does not go away across new sessions until the cache is refreshed. Editing the marketplace files does not propagate; the cache is what Claude Code appears to load at session start.\n\n## Remedy\n\nClear the plugin cache so Claude Code repopulates it from the marketplace on the next session.\n\n**Targeted (recommended):**\n\n```bash\nrm -rf ~/.claude/plugins/cache/lore-framework/\n```\n\nClears only the lore-framework cache; other plugins' caches (e.g. agoda-marketplace) remain intact and don't need to be re-resolved on next session.\n\n**Broader (fallback, if you suspect cross-plugin corruption):**\n\n```bash\nrm -rf ~/.claude/plugins/cache/\n```\n\nWipes every plugin's cache — Claude Code repopulates them all on the next session start. No permanent state is lost; only the locally cached copies of installed plugins are removed.\n\n**Workspace-local helper.** Some agent-repo workspaces ship a `./clear_plugin_cache.sh` script (e.g. the Activities workspace). It runs `rm -rf ~/.claude/plugins/cache/*`, which wipes the cache contents but preserves the `cache/` directory itself — a near-equivalent of the broader manual command above.\n\nThis is a destructive operation. Confirm with the user before running.\n\n**After clearing:**\n\n1. **Exit the current Claude Code session.** The cached state is held in memory for the duration of the session — even after wiping the cache, this session continues to see the old skill list.\n2. **Start a fresh session.** Claude Code re-resolves plugins from the marketplace, repopulates the cache, and the new skill list takes effect.\n3. **Verify.** Confirm the previously-missing skill now appears (e.g. type `/lr:workspace-pull` and check that the slash-command picker resolves it). Re-boot the agent and confirm any version-dependent boot output reflects the current `VERSION`.\n\n## Why It Happens\n\nClaude Code appears to resolve plugin content through `~/.claude/plugins/cache/` rather than reading the marketplace files on every session start: the cache directory holds the resolved plugin tree, and `installed_plugins.json` points its `installPath` at the cache, not the marketplace. In some upgrade scenarios the cache is not invalidated when the marketplace updates, leaving the whole prior-version plugin tree resident. This is most user-visible when the new version contains hard renames (a deleted directory plus a freshly named one) or removed skills, since those changes make the divergence concrete.\n\nA few common triggers:\n\n- A `/plugin update` ran but the cache wasn't invalidated for the affected plugin (race / partial-update case).\n- The user is developing the framework locally (`claude --plugin-dir ./lore-framework`) and switched between branches that have different skill catalogs without restarting.\n- A version bump that included **deletions** (e.g. v11's removal of `skills/pull-domain/`) — the cache still has the old directory.\n- Manual edits to cache contents (rare; for debugging) that get overwritten by a refresh in inconsistent ways.\n\nIn practice, the session also appears to load the available skill list once at start: even after wiping the cache mid-session, the running session continues to see the prior skill list — a fresh session is required for changes to take effect.\n\n## Prevention\n\nWhenever a framework migration or release note **adds, removes, or renames** a skill or `/lr-*` command — or **edits SKILL.md content** in a way that changes runtime behavior — the migration / release-notes doc must instruct the user to clear the plugin cache and restart Claude Code after applying the upgrade. See `docs/conventions.md` § Migration / Release-Note Authoring (the v12 cache-clear footer convention).\n\n## See Also\n\n- `docs/doctor.md` — orchestrator and ailment catalog.\n- `docs/doctor-cursor-session-without-plugin.md` — Cursor session with no plugin loaded (missing skills entirely, not stale content).\n- `docs/conventions.md` — the cache-clear footer convention authors must apply when shipping cache-affecting versions.\n- `docs/update.md` — `/lr:update` flow; cache-clear is a follow-up step after a version bump that changes skills.\n- `release-notes/12.md` — first release note that codifies the cache-clear convention.\nFor every agent found in step 4, verify that `role.md` has valid YAML frontmatter containing:\n- `description` — a non-empty string\n\nReport any agents with missing or malformed frontmatter fields.\n\nNote: `role.md` does not carry a `version` field at framework version 2+. Agent-level version stamping was removed — only `lore-repo.md` tracks the framework version, one per repo. If a `version` field is present in `role.md`, flag it as **informational** — the repo likely predates migration 2 and can be reconciled with `/lr:update`.\n\n## 6. Agent discovery vs registration\n\nFor each agent found in step 4, check whether an engine-native registered shortcut exists:\n\n- **Claude Code:** `lr-<agent-name>-agent.md` in `.claude/commands/`\n- **Codex:** `lr-<agent-name>-agent/` in `~/.codex/skills/` containing `SKILL.md`\n\nReport any agents without a registered shortcut as **informational** (registration is optional — agents are always loadable via `/lr:boot`).\n\nConversely, for every registered shortcut artifact found in those locations, verify the agent directory it references actually exists. Report any shortcuts pointing to missing agent directories as **errors**.\n\n## 7. Registered shortcut link validity\n\nFor every registered shortcut artifact:\n\n- **Claude Code:** `lr-*-agent.md` in `.claude/commands/`\n- **Codex:** `lr-*-agent/SKILL.md` in `~/.codex/skills/`\n\nExtract all file paths referenced in the content. Verify each path resolves to an existing file. Report any broken paths.\n\n## 8. Agent directory structure\n\nFor every agent found in step 4, verify the directory contains all required files and directories:\n- `role.md`\n- `lore-context.md`\n- `lore/` directory\n- `workdir/` directory\n\nReport any missing components.\n\n## 9. lore-context.md topic references\n\nFor every agent, read `lore-context.md` and extract any lore topic filenames referenced (e.g. `topic-name.md`). Verify each referenced file exists in the agent's `lore/` directory. Report any broken references.\n\n## 10. Lore topic cross-references\n\nFor every `.md` file in each agent's `lore/` directory, extract any `.md` filenames referenced in the content. Verify each referenced file exists in the same `lore/` directory. Report any broken references.\n\n## 11. lore-context.md size\n\nFor every agent, check the size of `lore-context.md`. Warn if it exceeds 40K tokens (approaching the 50K limit) or flag as a violation if it exceeds 50K tokens.\n\n## 12. Pending reflections\n\nFor every agent directory, check if a `reflections/` directory exists and is non-empty. If so, flag it: reflection has been run but merge has not — lore is not yet up to date.\n\n## 13. Uncommitted changes in lore files\n\nFor every lore agent repo in the workspace, run `git -C <lore-agent-repo> status` (where `<lore-agent-repo>` is the current iteration's repo path) to detect any lore files that are modified but not committed. Flag these: the knowledge exists only on the local filesystem and is not preserved in git history. This is especially critical for `lore-context.md`, `role.md`, and any `lore/` topic files.\n\nAlways use `git -C <lore-agent-repo>` rather than `cd`ing into each repo — the shell CWD is shared with Glob, Grep, and other git calls, and a `cd` here will silently shift subsequent checks' root.\n\n## 14. lore-context.md staleness (git timestamps)\n\nFor every agent, use `git -C <lore-agent-repo> log -1 --format=%ci -- <file>` to get the last commit date of `lore-context.md` and of each lore topic in `lore/`. If any topic was committed more recently than `lore-context.md`, flag it: the summary may not reflect the latest state of that topic. List the topic name and how far out of date the summary is.\n\n## 15. lore-context.md semantic consistency\n\nFor every agent, for each lore topic referenced in `lore-context.md`: read the topic file and compare its heading (first `#` line) and opening sentence against what `lore-context.md` says about it. Flag any cases where the topic's actual title or subject clearly differs from the description in lore-context — this indicates the summary was not updated after the topic was substantially revised.\n\n## 16. Registered shortcut vs role.md\n\nFor every registered shortcut artifact, compare its last modification date against the last commit date of the agent's `role.md`. If `role.md` was updated more recently, flag it: the shortcut may not accurately describe the agent's current role. Also do a quick semantic check: verify the agent name in the shortcut matches the heading in `role.md`.\n\n## 17. Orphaned pre-plugin skill commands\n\nScan `<workspace>/.claude/commands/` for files matching `lr-*.md` that do **not** match `lr-*-agent.md` AND whose content does **not** contain the phrase `boot as agent`. For each such file, extract `<skill-name>` from the filename (strip the `lr-` prefix and `.md` suffix) and check whether `<framework-root>/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` exists.\n\n- If the plugin skill exists, flag the file as an **orphaned pre-plugin skill duplicate** — `/lr:<skill-name>` is now provided by the plugin, so the local command is redundant and typically references stale sibling paths (`lore-framework/docs/...`). Report the file path and the covering plugin skill. Suggest: run `/lr:update` (migration 5 prompts to delete these per file) or delete manually.\n- If no matching plugin skill exists, the file is a user-authored command — do not flag it.\n\n## 18. Legacy registered shortcut formats\n\nFor every Claude shortcut file `lr-*-agent.md` in `<workspace>/.claude/commands/` whose content contains `boot as agent`, check the format. The current Claude form uses absolute paths and includes the agent directory:\n\n```\nRead `<absolute-path>/docs/agent-boot.md` and boot as agent `<agent-name>` from `<absolute-agent-dir>`.\n```\n\nFlag any Claude file that instead uses:\n- `lore-framework/docs/agent-boot.md` (pre-v5 sibling-path form)\n- `<framework-root>/docs/agent-boot.md` (v5 form — unresolved in `.claude/commands/`)\n- Any form lacking the `from <agent-dir>` suffix\n\nThese legacy Claude formats cause slower or broken boots. Suggest: run `/lr:update` (migration 6 regenerates them) or re-register with `/lr:register-repo`.\n\nFor every Codex shortcut skill `lr-*-agent/SKILL.md` in `~/.codex/skills/` whose content contains\n`boot as agent`, flag it if it lacks the `from <agent-dir>` suffix or does not point at an\nabsolute `agent-boot.md` path. These comments **are** the\n  normative procedure (see § Literate Accelerator below); no behavioral change.\n- `docs/agent-boot.md` — happy path delegates to `lr-core preflight`; § Manual Boot Procedure no\n  longer restates the steps in prose — it points at `cmd_preflight`'s docstring and the three\n  helper functions it names.\n- `docs/attach.md` — guest discovery, pull, and version comparison collapse into one preflight\n  call; the failure-path pointer names `_resolve_agent`/`pull_repo`/`compare_versions` instead of\n  restating their steps.\n- `docs/consult.md` — host-side existence check uses `lr-core discover` to fail fast on a typo;\n  failure path points at `cmd_discover`'s docstring.\n- `docs/pull-lore.md`, `docs/process-merge.md` — auto-pull sites call preflight with `--fresh`;\n  failure path points directly at `pull_repo`'s comments.\n- `docs/lore-search.md` — search briefs carry a `scan` manifest.\n- `docs/auto-pull.md` — cut from 96 to ~85 lines: the hand-executed pull steps (bare-repo\n  handling, fail-fast env vars, the TTL stamp) moved into `pull_repo()`'s own comments; this doc\n  keeps only what's genuinely caller-side policy (the per-site reporting-verbosity table) plus\n  conceptual framing (Worktrees, Invariants, Distinct From) that isn't duplicated by the script.\n- `docs/version-check.md` — boot step references renumbered to match the new boot procedure.\n- `docs/trilens-loop.md` — **rewritten from 325 lines to 80.** The procedure is unchanged in\n  intent (resolve scope → three cold independent reviewers, one per lens → triage and apply →\n  repeat with fresh reviewers until a round is clean, ceiling of 3) and the rails it names are\n  unchanged (cold-context reviewers only, no host-side fallback, regular-tier reviewer models, the\n  disposition ledger carried between rounds, a silent round is not a clean round, never finish on an\n  outstanding `BLOCK`, disclose anything you turn off). What is gone is the long-form elaboration:\n  the per-engine spawn guidance and the worked examples. What is **new** is an explicit exchange contract — the host\n  sends a reviewer only the trees, the changed-file list, a sentence of orientation and its lens,\n  and gets back only findings-as-pointers (path, line, signature, a paragraph, a severity) plus a\n  verdict. No diffs or file contents cross the wire in either direction, at any scale. **If you rely\n  on `/lr:trilens-loop` behaving exactly as it did in v30, re-read the doc before your next run.**\n  **Correction carried forward:** the Codex regular-tier reviewer model is **`gpt-5.4`**.\n  `release-notes/30.md` named it `gpt-4.5`, which was wrong; v30's notes are left as shipped and this\n  entry is the correction of record.\n- `docs/being.md`, `docs/takeover.md`, `docs/wait.md`, `docs/workspace-pull.md` — one-line Script\n  Fallback Contract pointers at their script-delegation sites (unaffected by the literate-\n  accelerator change — these are all Implementation scripts).\n- `docs/spawn-teammate.md`, `docs/teammate-conventions.md` — teammate-rule loading now cites\n  `agent-boot.md` Step 2 (was Step 5 before the boot doc was renumbered).\n- `docs/conventions.md` — § Script Fallback Contract's Accelerator category redefined as\n  **literate**: the procedure lives in the script's own comments, not a companion doc (see below);\n  § Tooling: Non-Shell Runtimes gains the deterministic-substrate class alongside the protocol-\n  server one.\n\n### Literate Accelerator\n\nAn accelerator script's procedure now lives in its own instructional comments — docstrings and\ninline `# Step N:` blocks written so a reader could execute each step without running the code —\nrather than in a separate prose doc. This removes the last drift risk in the accelerator model:\npreviously the same procedure existed twice (once as code, once as doc prose), and the two could\ndiverge from each other. `scripts/lr-core` is the first and, so far, only instance. See\n`docs/conventions.md` § Script Fallback Contract for the rule, and the lore-architect's\n`literate-accelerator-pattern.md` for the fuller writeup.\n\n## Compatibility\n\nNo repo migration, and no change to the shape of an agent repo. An install whose `python3` is\nmissing or whose cache is stale keeps working through the fallback path.\n\nThree behavior changes are worth knowing about, none of them breaking:\n\n- **Pull freshness.** A pull that succeeded within the TTL window (default 600s) is now reported\n  `fresh` and skipped, where v30 always hit the network. Attach and consult moments after a boot\n  are the common case. Pass `--fresh` (or use `/lr:pull-lore`) to force the round-trip.\n- **Teammate detection** now walks up to six process ancestors instead of inspecting only the\n  immediate parent, and matches `--agent-id` on a flag boundary. This detects spawns that v30\n  missed through a wrapper process; it does not change what a detected teammate then does.\n- **`/lr:trilens-loop`** runs from a rewritten, much shorter procedure doc — same rails, far less\n  elaboration. See § What Changed.\n\nAuto-pull is also now stricter in one place: a lore repo that is not the root of its own git\nrepository is `skipped` rather than pulled. See `release-notes/31.md`, `v31-lr-core-parked-2026-07-25.md`, and `lifecycle-harness-plugin-identity-unverified.md`.\n\n## Backfill discipline\n\nEvery finalization that lands a `VERSION` bump must add the new version's entry here — including kind, scope summary, and cache-affecting annotation. Backfill at the same finalization that ships the version is the principled timing — not \"we'll get to it later.\" Drift in the history list erodes the topic's value as a per-version classification index.\n\n**Scan the whole tail for gaps, not just the current version — the discipline is not self-healing (v21 lesson).** Appending only the current version's entry each ship silently carries forward any gap a prior slipped ship left. Landing v21 (2026-07-06), I found the history was missing **both** v20 and v21 — the v20 ship had slipped the backfill entirely, and appending only v21 would have left the v20 gap permanent. So at every ship, before adding the new entry, scan the tail between the last recorded version and the one shipping and backfill **all** missing entries in the same ship. Cheap check: `for v in <last+1>..<current>; do grep -c \"v$v \" versioning-release-types.md; done` — any `0` is a gap. This is a bounded mechanical sweep, so it belongs in the current ship (`feedback-don-t-defer-completable-scope.md`). `/lr:check` has no check for this yet — a candidate: assert a history entry exists for every `release-notes/<N>.md` / `migrations/<N>.md` (see `consistency-checks.md`).\n\nThis discipline composes with the deferral-discipline rule (`feedback-don-t-defer-completable-scope.md`): the backfill is a bounded mechanical task that fits in the current ship's scope. It also composes with the cache-clear-footer convention: the same finalization should both (a) ensure the release-notes has the footer if applicable, and (b) record the cache-affecting status in this history list.\n\nThe role.md responsibilities call this out explicitly — see `role.md` § Lore-Curation Disciplines.\n\n**\"Commit pending\" can accumulate across versions — verify `git HEAD` at session start.** When lore\nsays a version is \"built, commit pending,\" don't assume the last-described version is the committed\none. At the start of the v18/v19 ship, the public repo `HEAD` was still at v17 — *both* v18 (lr-wait,\nrecorded as \"commit pending\") and the whole port were uncommitted in one working tree, so shipping\nrequired untangling and committing in order (v18 first, then v19), not a single push. Ground the\ncurrent state in `git log`/`git HEAD`, not in the most recent lore entry (a `verify-before-acting`\ninstance — `verify-before-acting-on-suspected-bugs.md`).\n\n## In-band BETA refinement (post-v10 observation)\n\nWhen a BETA feature needs refinement after its initial release, the version-bump ceremony is **not** required. Pattern:\n\n1. **Edit the procedure doc** (`docs/<feature>.md`) — source of truth for current behavior.\n2. **Leave the release notes alone** (`release-notes/<N>.md`) — they're a historical record, frozen at the version they describe. A verbatim citation that goes stale post-refinement is acceptable.\n3. **No `VERSION` bump** — the BETA caveat (\"internal procedure may evolve based on real-world usage\") in the release notes is the contract that licenses this.\n4. **Update lore at finalization** — design-decisions topics for the feature reflect the *current* state, not the originally-shipped state.\n\nWhen the feature graduates from BETA, the graduation release notes describe the cumulative final state, not each iteration. Stable (non-BETA) features need a different cadence — refinements there are full release-notes events with version bumps.\n\n**When to break this pattern** (not yet observed; anticipated):\n\n- **Breaking change within BETA** — if existing usage will fail in a non-obvious way, mark explicitly with release notes + bump.\n- **New state, file format, or per-agent metadata** — needs migration tracking regardless of stability label.\n- **Refinement large enough to be a new feature** — graduate the BETA or treat as v(N+1).\n"
